question: Does the heldout site log-score delta depend on chronological detection order after site n and k are fixed?
derivation: Both fitted candidate models have exchangeable within-site daily Bernoulli observations: site score is a function of n_i and k_i only; detection ordering is not in likelihood. For any permutation of observed 0/1 within site with NA positions fixed, site log-score and CV fold training fit are exactly invariant up to numerical tolerance.
tests: recompute fixed 5-fold original heldout site scores
199 site-wise order permutations, preserving NA and each site's n,k
verify all site log-score deltas unchanged to 1e-6 without refit, by sufficient-statistic identity
recalculate adjacent switching and its Spearman correlation to unchanged site score delta for each permutation
compare original rho to permutation distribution (two-sided empirical +1 p); do not interpret naive unconditioned rho p as biological evidence
limits: This is an internal structural negative control, not independent ecological evidence
Switching is not an explanatory input to either model
No measured A/B/M, effort or closure; no EOG-WF endpoint
